races.title: State Assembly, District 18
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Andre Sandford
cands.bio: Housing program manager who has worked in social services, including child protective services, foster care, transition-age youth services, clinical mental health management and housing management. Ran for California State Assembly District 18 in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Forward Party of California endorsed him in both 2024 and 2026. Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide also recommended him in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was raised or when he moved to California. We found no record of any elected office or legislative work. We found no statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his stated positions come only from his 2024 survey. We found no documented deeds on any of these topics. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages available.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He reports over eight years in social services and leadership, including child protective services, foster care, transition-age youth services, clinical mental health management and housing management. He is currently a program manager for housing and homelessness prevention at a San Francisco nonprofit. He holds no elected office.
qual.why: He has a real work record in housing and social services, which is relevant to policy. He has no legislative service, no local elected office, and no documented budget or law career, so he scores in the low-middle range.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he would restore and increase funding for policing and make sure officers have the tools and training they need.

land-for-floridians.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he would tax corporations that buy homes and pursue an Anti-Trust Act expansion so that 80% of homes are reserved for families.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he would reduce building permits for single-family homes.

cands.name: Mia Bonta
cands.bio: Democrat serving in the California State Assembly for District 18 (Oakland, Alameda, Emeryville) since 2021. Former CEO of Oakland Promise, a nonprofit, and former president of the Alameda Unified School District Board. Holds degrees from Yale, Harvard Graduate School of Education and Yale Law School. Chairs the Assembly Health Committee.

controversies.text: In June 2021, while Mia Bonta ran in the special election for her husband's Assembly seat, rival Janani Ramachandran said gaming-industry donations to her campaign might be meant to influence her husband, Attorney General Rob Bonta. The San Francisco Chronicle reported no finding of wrongdoing.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.

cands.gaps: We could not establish where she was raised. Wikipedia says only that her mother was a working mother in the Bronx, and she says she moved 13 times in 16 years. We found no record of specific bills she authored or actions she took on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, police pay, gun laws or school choice. Her campaign site describes legislation she says she passed, such as drug price gouging and protections for minors facing deportation, but the pages we read give no bill numbers or official records. We found no documented stances from her on data centers or development. We could not read the details of the 2021 claims about gambling-industry money beyond a one-line summary.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born in New York City and said in 2021 that she moved to Alameda more than 20 years earlier, after finishing law school in 1999, which puts her arrival as an adult about 25 or more years ago.

qual.background: Member of the California Assembly since 2021 and re-elected several times. Previously CEO of Oakland Promise and elected to the Alameda school board in 2018, becoming its president. Holds a J.D. from Yale Law School and sits on the Assembly Budget Committee.
qual.why: About five years of prior legislative service, local elected office, a nonprofit executive career and a law degree put her in the high range for writing law and the state budget. Committee seats and chairing the Health Committee were not counted.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site says she is fighting to protect East Bay families from federal overreach and unjust deportation, and says every person in the community deserves to live without fear.
